_about: Synthetic scenarios for the Conversational Core v1 A/B comparison.
Every message here was written for this file. Nothing is copied from a real
conversation, a chat export or an agency document, and no scenario names a
The format is the one services/trajectory_eval.py already loads, so these
run through the same harness as eval/trajectories.json. Two extra keys are
read by the A/B runner and ignored by the loader: 'id', the stable scenario
identifier used in run artifacts and the blind review, and 'rubric_focus',
which names the review dimensions a scenario was built to exercise.
Most scenarios are deliberately non-commercial. The first Core v1 increment
is a conversational change, and a suite where every scenario ends in a sale
would measure the commercial path instead of the thing being changed.

suites._about: Named subsets. 'conversational' is the one the first Core v1 increment is aimed at; 'commercial' is kept separate so a conversational change is not judged on the commercial path; 'smoke' is two short scenarios for checking that a run works at all.

trajectories.name: an ordinary statement that needs a reaction, not a question
trajectories.covers: A plain statement with nothing to resolve. A reaction or a contribution is a complete reply; a question here is the forced-question habit. Catches generic validation and the paraphrase-validate-ask loop.

turns.tests: a closing beat; does the reply add something or reach for a question

turns.message: yeah pretty much
turns.tests: flat agreement after a closing beat; does the conversation continue or restart

trajectories.name: a shared imagined scene, then an indirect reference back to it
trajectories.covers: Several turns build a hypothetical the two of them are inventing together. A later turn refers to one of its elements obliquely. Tests scene continuity, reference resolution, contribution to the scene, and whether vivid shared imagination is correctly not treated as a claim about the real world.

turns.tests: the scene is explicitly framed as imagined

trajectories.covers: Four turns on one subject, then a clean pivot to another. Tests cheap adaptation: no dragging the old trajectory along, no repeated steering back, and no throwing away everything that still applies.

trajectories.covers: The fan states something, the conversation proceeds, and then the fan explicitly corrects it. Tests whether later replies honour the correction and whether the superseded belief comes back as though it were true.

trajectories.covers: Two simulated absences inside one conversation. Tests natural resumption, a relevant callback to what was open, and specifically that the creator does not invent a present-tense claim about what it is doing right now.

trajectories.name: the fan asks to see more, in the middle of an ordinary conversation
trajectories.covers: Interest arises from the conversation rather than from an offer. Tests whether the transition stays conversational, avoids catalogue copy, avoids exposing package or media detail, and keeps fan-visible wording separate from the operation underneath.

turns.message: nice. what were you actually doing that afternoon
turns.tests: back to conversation; does the commercial moment end cleanly

trajectories.name: the fan declines and wants to keep talking
trajectories.covers: A refusal in the middle of a conversation the fan is enjoying. Tests that a no is accepted without a pressure loop or an immediate second offer, and that the conversation can continue naturally afterwards.

trajectories.name: a direct media request inside the paid private chat
trajectories.covers: A fan repeatedly asks to see creator-controlled content while an intimate line develops. Tests that Cleopatra knows the fan is already in the private chat, considers real offer/delivery affordances, never narrates an attachment into existence, and keeps unsupported creator actions explicitly imagined.

turns.message: i really need to see more of you
turns.tests: direct visual request; a real same-chat offer may be natural, but redirecting to another DM or pretending media appeared is not

turns.message: spicy for sure, i'm really in the mood
turns.tests: intimacy alone must not force a sale

turns.message: i trust your judgement, pick something
turns.tests: fan delegates content choice; actual media affordances should be considered without inventing inventory

turns.message: i'm all ready baby
turns.tests: text or shared imagination may continue, but present-world creator actions need evidence

turns.message: show me baby, i really want to see it
turns.tests: repeated direct media request; choose a legal operation or honest text, never prose-only delivery
